frequency_question: How often do major bipartisan permitting reform bills successfully pass both chambers and receive the President's signature during a high-polarization congressional session?
membership_rule: Includes major legislative packages explicitly focused on energy permitting reform or infrastructure streamlining with cross-party compromise attempts; excludes narrow appropriations riders or non-energy infrastructure bills.

cases.name: Manchin Permitting Reform Bill Attempts (Inflation Reduction Act side deal)
The Fiscal Responsibility Act Permitting Provisions

coverage_note: 3 named major legislative push cycles; captures the primary modern attempts at comprehensive or substantial energy permitting reform.
known_gaps: Smaller incremental riders attached to National Defense Authorization Acts or omnibus appropriations are excluded as they do not constitute 'comprehensive' reform.
skeleton: Three major legislative push cycles for permitting reform in divided or narrow-majority control contexts over the last thirty years, yielding 2 hits out of 3 distinct high-salience legislative vehicles.
validity_reason: The base rate depends on partisan polarization and legislative filibuster norms, which remain stable across current congressional structures through the end of the decade.
